chunks: And it has indeed been narrated:

“Indeed, wudu (ablution) is a limit among the limits set by Allah, so that Allah may know who obeys Him and who disobeys Him. And indeed, nothing renders the believer impure; rather, something like oil is sufficient for him.”

key_terms.الدَّهْنِ: oil, used here to indicate a small and slight amount
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer, whose essential state is not made impure by external contact
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual act of purification before worship
key_terms.حَدٌّ: a prescribed limit or ordinance set by Allah
key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the divinely established limits and ordinances
key_terms.يَعْصِيهِ: disobeys Him, by going against Allah’s command
key_terms.يُطِيعُهُ: obeys Him, by complying with Allah’s command

ai.seo_question: Why is wudu described as one of Allah’s limits, and how much water is sufficient for it?
ai.summary: This hadith presents wudu (ablution) as one of the divinely ordained limits through which obedience and disobedience are manifested. It also indicates that the believer is not essentially defiled by external things, and that a minimal amount of water, like oil in smallness, is sufficient for wudu.
